value: ethylene production rhythmic, peaking near the middle of the light period and low at night
method: ethylene in the headspace of seedling tubes measured every 3 h by gas chromatography

quote: Both cultivars showed rhythmic ethylene production with peaks near the middle of the light period and low ethylene, production at night.
note: A daily rhythm of a hormone output in seedlings, not of movement; both cultivars (wild type and phytochrome B mutant).

source.authors: Finlayson SA, Lee IJ, Morgan PW
source.title: Phytochrome B and the Regulation of Circadian Ethylene Production in Sorghum1

value: under 4 h light:20 h dark the ethylene rhythm anticipated the light/warm period
method: ethylene in the headspace of seedling tubes measured every 3 h by gas chromatography
quote: Plants grown under extremely short photo-/thermoperiods (4 h light:20 h dark) also showed a rhythmic production of ethylene, which anticipated the appearance of the light/warm period (Fig. 1 C).
note: The Discussion reads the predawn rise as anticipation of the light period by the clock.

source.authors: Finlayson SA, Lee IJ, Morgan PW
source.title: Phytochrome B and the Regulation of Circadian Ethylene Production in Sorghum1

value: ethylene rhythm free-running in constant light and temperature, period approximately 24 h
method: seedlings entrained for 2 d under 12-h photo-/thermoperiods, then held in constant light and temperature; ethylene measured every 3 h
conditions: constant light and temperature after entrainment
quote: Figure 2 A shows that the ethylene rhythm is free-running in both cultivars, with strong peaks produced by cv 58M occurring within an approximate 24-h period.
note: Shows an endogenous circadian clock behind the daily ethylene rhythm; cv 58M is the phytochrome B null mutant, whose peaks are the clearest.

source.authors: Finlayson SA, Lee IJ, Morgan PW
source.title: Phytochrome B and the Regulation of Circadian Ethylene Production in Sorghum1

value: light or temperature cycles alone drive a daily ethylene rhythm, but circadian entrainment requires both light and temperature cycles
method: seedlings grown under light cycles, temperature cycles or both, then released into constant conditions
conditions: 12-h photoperiods and/or 12-h thermoperiods (31/22 °C) before constant conditions
quote: The diurnal rhythm can be produced with either light or temperature cycles; however, both light and temperature cycles are required for circadian entrainment.
note: Results: seedlings entrained by light cycles alone at constant 26 °C, or by temperature cycles alone in constant light, did not keep cycling in constant conditions.

source.authors: Finlayson SA, Lee IJ, Morgan PW
source.title: Phytochrome B and the Regulation of Circadian Ethylene Production in Sorghum1

value: temperature overrides light in timing the daily ethylene rhythm: with warm nights and cool days, ethylene peaks came during the warm nights
method: seedlings grown under 12-h photoperiods with the thermoperiod reversed (warm dark period, cool light period)
conditions: reversed photo- and thermoperiods (warm nights, cool days)
quote: The temperature signal overrides the light signal in the production of diurnal rhythms, because seedlings grown under thermoperiods reversed with the photoperiod produced ethylene peaks during the warm nights.

source.authors: Finlayson SA, Lee IJ, Morgan PW

value: phytochrome B null mutant produces rhythmic ethylene peaks with about 10 times the wild-type amplitude, with the same period and timing
method: comparison of near-isogenic wild-type (cv 100M, PHYB) and phytochrome B null mutant (cv 58M, phyB-1) seedlings; ethylene every 3 h
quote: The phytochrome B mutant produces rhythmic peaks of ethylene with approximately 10 times the amplitude of the wild-type counterpart with the same period and diurnal timing.
note: Phytochrome B (a red/far-red light receptor) damps the amplitude of the rhythm; the paper concludes it is not required for circadian timing itself. Results add that the extra ethylene comes from the shoot (Table I).

value: dim, far-red-enriched light reproduced the phytochrome B mutant's shade-avoidance phenotype and ethylene peaks in the wild type
method: wild-type and mutant seedlings grown under dim, far-red-enriched incandescent light compared with fluorescent plus incandescent light
conditions: dim light 29 μmol m−2 s−1 PAR, red:far-red 0.75, versus 225 μmol m−2 s−1 PAR, red:far-red 1.42; 12-h photo-/thermoperiods
quote: This treatment duplicated the phytochrome B mutant's shade-avoidance phenotype in the wild type and caused the wild type to produce ethylene peaks similar to those observed in the mutant.
note: A shade response through the red to far-red ratio of the light. The light figures in conditions are given in Materials and Methods.
